chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz ibn Abdillah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
«The camel is left loose in the Haram (sanctuary), eating whatever it wishes.» And it has been permitted to pluck the idhkhir and the two branches of al-mahalah.

key_terms.اَلْإِذْخِرِ: Idhkhir, a type of aromatic plant found in Mecca
key_terms.اَلْحَرَمِ: The Sanctuary (Mecca), a sacred area with specific rules for pilgrims
key_terms.اَلْمَحَالَةِ: Al-mahalah, a type of shrub or branch

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for an animal in ihram within the Haram sanctuary and which plants are permitted to be plucked?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific exemptions for pilgrims in the Haram sanctuary, distinguishing between general prohibitions and permitted acts like grazing camels and plucking idhkhir and mahalah. It reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of flexibility within the sanctity of Mecca, allowing for necessary sustenance and minor actions that do not violate the core spirit of ihram.
